messages.author: fb40a65bd21dcf6f
messages.subject: Eigenvalue decomposition of covariance matrix
parts:
Hi,
Suppose I have several multivariate Gaussians x_i ~ N(0, Sigma_i) but all the Sigma_i are weighted sums of a base covariance K and some noise:

Sigma_i = alpha_i K + eps_i I

K is also probably low rank. This setting lends itself to an eigendecomposition of K=QVQ' (Q orthogonal, V diagonal) from which the inverses of all the Sigma_i can be easily calculated:

Sigma_i^-1 = Q(alpha_i V + eps_i I)Q'

I know I can call eigenvalues_sym and eigenvectors_sym to calculate Q and V but will this do the calculation twice? There does not seem to be any support for sharing the results between calls.

Also is there any way to take advantage of the low rank of K (perhaps by doing a partial eigendecomposition)?

Thanks,
John.

P.S. I think I will see some readers of this list in Lenzerheide so I'm looking forward to that one.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Eigenvalue decomposition of covariance matrix
parts:
Trying to fit to low rank structure is a minefield — it’s much
better to encode low rank structure in the model from the
beginning.  There has been lots of work on low-rank GPs
recently — implementing them in Stan is not trivial due to
our lack of some structured linear algebra operations, but it’s
possible.
